text:
For a slim Qi2 power bank for the iPhone 17, I'd pick the **Anker Nano Power Bank (5K, MagGo, Slim)**. It costs $54.99 and 9to5Mac's June 2026 roundup named it the best slim pick.

**[Anker Nano Power Bank 5K, buy at Anker US](https://www.anker.com/products/a1665-5k-ultra-slim-qi2-power-bank)**
- It's 0.34 in (8.6 mm) thick and weighs 4.3 oz (122 g), according to Anker's page.
- It holds 5,000mAh, which Anker says delivers roughly 2,750–3,500mAh after conversion loss. That's well under one full iPhone charge, so think of it as a top-up.
- It charges at up to 15W wirelessly on iPhone 12 through 17. 9to5Mac calls it the closest alternative to Apple's MagSafe battery and the fastest of the slim options.
- Anker's page is inconsistent on a couple of points. It says both "Qi2-Compatible" and "Qi2-Certified," and one output line lists wireless at 5W max. The 15W figure appears in the compatibility section and in 9to5Mac's review.

**Other options**
- **Cheaper and thin:** The [Baseus MagSafe battery](https://9to5mac.com/2026/06/27/favorite-magsafe-iphone-battery-banks-right-now/) costs $24.99 and is about as thin as the Anker. It isn't Qi2 and charges at only 7.5W. I couldn't find a direct product page, so the link goes to the 9to5Mac roundup that covers it.
- **More capacity, with a trade-off:** The UGREEN 10,000mAh costs $59.99 and charges at up to 25W (Qi2.2, iPhone 16 or later). 9to5Mac says it's thicker than the others. The Belkin 25W 10,000mAh costs $99.99 and is "a little chunky," so it isn't slim.
- **LISEN P601:** This is a 5,000mAh, 15W Qi2 bank listed at 0.38 in thick. I didn't verify its details or price. [Product page](https://lisenintl.com/products/p601-magsafe-power-bank/).
- **Baseus PicoGo AM52:** A 10,000mAh, 45W Qi2.2 bank. A deal site lists code AM52 for $6 off ($59.99 → $53.99) at Baseus's US store. I didn't confirm its thickness, so it may not be truly slim. [Deal page](https://dealectric.com/lab/V3/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w).

**What I couldn't check:** The Android Central test of 2026 slim banks (Baseus, TORRAS, INIU, ReelCharge) loaded only its title, so I haven't used it. The Wired page wouldn't load either. Neither Macworld nor Wired informed this answer.

Choose the Anker if you want the slimmest, fastest-charging option. If you'd rather have a full charge or more, the UGREEN 10,000mAh is the better fit, and it gives up some slimness.
